candidates.name: closed-citation-priority
candidates.mechanism: Complete cited source regions at the best actual parent rank receive one length-independent vote in an earlier tier, then the original focus selector fills the remainder.

candidates.name: source-concept-coverage
candidates.mechanism: Original source lexical concepts share saturating value across occurrences; actual source cue ranks are retained, without a character multiplier. Original cost closures and wire checks remain.

candidates.name: cue-piece-count
candidates.mechanism: Only remove the character multiplier from existing disjoint cue-piece weights. Preserve candidate units, costs, ranks, original coordinates and semantic scores.

scope: Six-stage development delivery ablations over the identical saved histories; no answering-model or token-reduction result, no production adoption.
hypothesisBoundaries: Whole-citation priority can shift missing code elsewhere. It does not establish that every citation must be shipped in full.
Shared lexical concepts are an incomplete proxy for distinct source conditions; higher proxy coverage cannot substitute for actual original code.
Counting existing disjoint cue pieces without length changes their subdivision sensitivity; failure does not rule out every length-independent objective.
The earlier closed-demand replay changed the value domain to whole prerequisite closures and is distinct from the one-line cue-piece ablation.
